anchors.description: Outer-frame horizontal width of the bottom-right ground-floor arched window, measured between the outer edge of the left window jamb and the outer edge of the right window jamb at the same height (image row y=600): frame-to-wall boundary at x~1076.5 and x~1235.0.
anchors.visible_evidence: The same polychrome brick wall flanking the window shows an English-bond lattice: header courses with vertical joints every ~11.7 px (2D autocorrelation peak dx=12, dy=0) and stretcher courses with joints every ~23.5 px (peaks 23-24 px), i.e. a 2:1 length:width brick ratio. The window clear span at the same course line is 158.6 px, equal to 13.5 header modules or 6.7 stretcher modules. Vertical course pitch is ~6.9 px, consistent with the same metric brick format (ratio width:height ~1.7-1.8).
anchors.identity_uncertainty: The exact historic brick format is not identified: Reichsformat 250x120x65 mm gives ~1.74 m, Normalformat 240x115x71 mm ~1.66 m, Dutch Waalformat 210x100x50 mm ~1.50 m, so the format alone spans roughly 1.5-2.0 m; edge blur and the slightly skewed window frame add about +/-0.05 m.
